chapter_title: Before We Go, Part 2: Traveling Well and the Learning for All Thread
learning_objective: The learner will interpret monthly temperature and rainfall charts for six stops on our route to predict November conditions, answering at least 3 of 4 prediction questions correctly before the answer is revealed.
specification:
Type: chart **sim-id:** november-weather-at-our-stops
**Library:** Chart.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Understand
**Bloom Verb:** interpret
**Learning Objective:** The learner will interpret monthly temperature and rainfall charts for six stops on our route to predict November conditions, answering at least 3 of 4 prediction questions correctly before the answer is revealed. **Prerequisites:** climate, Mediterranean climate (hot dry summers, mild wet winters), November as the start of the wet season, mean daily high and low temperature (defined in the sections "The Mediterranean Climate" and "November Weather" above). **Evidence of Mastery:** The learner answers four prediction questions, each locked in before the chart reveals the answer. An answer is correct when it matches the value computed from the data under Rules. Mastery is 3 of 4 correct. Switching stops and hovering over bars is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) The Mediterranean is warm and sunny all year. (2) Istanbul has the same weather as Athens because both are "Mediterranean." (3) Winter rain means it rains every day. (4) Summer is the wet season, as in many northern climates. **Instructional Rationale:** Interpreting a climate chart is an Understand-level skill; predicting before the reveal makes the learner read the chart's pattern rather than look up a number, and the four questions target the four misconceptions. **Content:** Six stops and the Wikipedia article whose climate table supplies their data: | Stop | Days on our trip | Source article | |---|---|---| | Istanbul | 1–5 | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Istanbul | | Çanakkale (Troy and Gallipoli) | 6 | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%87anakkale | | İzmir (nearest major station to Ephesus) | 7 | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C4%B0zmir | | Rhodes | 8 | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodes | | Heraklion | 9 | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heraklion | | Athens | 10–13 | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athens | For each stop, twelve monthly values of mean daily maximum temperature (°C), mean daily minimum temperature (°C), and mean monthly precipitation (mm). Temperatures are also shown in °F. November is visibly marked on every chart as "our month." Prediction questions, in this order: | # | Question | Choices | How the correct answer is found | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | Which stop has the coolest November afternoons? | Istanbul; Çanakkale; İzmir; Rhodes; Heraklion; Athens | The stop with the lowest November mean daily maximum | | 2 | In Athens, is November wetter or drier than August? | Wetter; Drier; About the same | Compare Athens November and August precipitation | | 3 | Which is the hottest month in Athens? | June; July; August; September | The month with the highest Athens mean daily maximum | | 4 | How much colder is a November night in Istanbul than a November afternoon in Heraklion? | 0–4 °C; 5–9 °C; 10–14 °C; 15 °C or more | Heraklion November mean daily maximum minus Istanbul November mean daily minimum | **Provenance:** From each source article, take the first "Climate data for ..." table, and copy into the sim folder the station name, the normal period (1991–2020 where the table gives it), and the twelve monthly values of mean daily maximum, mean daily minimum, and mean precipitation. Record the station and period under each chart. If the İzmir article's first table is not for İzmir itself, use the one that is. Do not fill in any value from memory. **Rules:** °F = °C × 9/5 + 32, rounded to the nearest whole degree. Question 2: "About the same" is correct when the two values differ by less than 10 mm; otherwise "Wetter" or "Drier" by the comparison. Question 3: if two months tie to 0.1 °C, both are accepted. Question 4: the difference is rounded to the nearest whole degree before choosing its band; a band's lower bound is inclusive (10.0 °C is in 10–14 °C). **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner reads question 1 and chooses an answer before any chart is shown. 2. The chart appears with all six stops' November highs side by side, and the correct answer is marked. 3. For questions 2–4, the learner chooses an answer, then the relevant chart is revealed (Athens monthly rainfall; Athens monthly highs; Istanbul and Heraklion November values). 4. After the four questions, free exploration unlocks: the learner chooses any stop and sees its twelve-month temperature lines and rainfall bars, with November marked. 5. The learner should notice the near-rainless summer and the jump in rain from October to November at every stop. **Feedback:** Four questions, fixed order, one attempt each. Correct: "Right. ." Incorrect: "Not quite. — ." Each explanation names the misconception the question targets: (1) the northern stops on the Turkish straits are cooler than the Aegean and Cretan stops; (2) the Mediterranean summer is dry and November starts the wet season; (3) the hottest month comes after the summer solstice; (4) a cool evening in Istanbul and a warm afternoon on Crete need different layers. A score "Predictions correct: n of 4" is shown. **Starting State:** Question 1 with its six choices and no chart yet, under the prompt "We'll be in all six places in November. Where should we pack the warmest layer for?" **Chapter Anchors:** Six stops. Istanbul and Çanakkale are the coolest, with November afternoons around 15–16 °C (59–61 °F); Athens, Rhodes and Heraklion around 19–21 °C (66–70 °F); nights about 6–8 °C cooler than afternoons. If the copied data disagree with any of these prose values, flag the difference to the author rather than changing the data.
